articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting Requirements
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) concerning the blocking and rejecting of transactions and the filing of reports with OFAC. This update provides further guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.

The amendments aim to clarify existing policies and procedures, ensuring that U.S. persons and entities can effectively navigate the complexities of sanctions compliance. These FAQs are crucial for understanding the nuances of reporting blocked property and rejected transactions, which are fundamental aspects of OFAC's enforcement framework.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Amends FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. This action reflects ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy in response to evolving geopolitical landscapes.

In conjunction with these designations and removals, OFAC also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions. These updates provide critical guidance for navigating permitted activities and compliance requirements under the modified sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Designations Under Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA)
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has implemented new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA). This action targets entities and individuals involved in the theft of American intellectual property, underscoring the U.S. commitment to safeguarding its technological and economic interests.

The designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses, which aim to mitigate unintended consequences and provide clarity for legitimate transactions. China's Ministry of Commerce has urged the U.S. to lift these sanctions, stating that they infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question. This update modifies existing authorizations pertaining to transactions involving Venezuela, reflecting ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy in the region.

The amendment provides further clarification and potentially alters the scope of permissible activities for U.S. persons and entities engaging with Venezuela. Stakeholders are advised to review the updated guidance to ensure continued compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran and Cuba Designations, Issues New and Amended General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting entities and individuals related to Iran and Cuba. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to address perceived threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC has also issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions. These documents provide crucial details on the scope of the sanctions and any authorized transactions, requiring careful review by affected parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation. This action indicates a specific adjustment to the sanctions program concerning Venezuela, potentially easing restrictions on the delisted entity or individual.

Such removals are typically a result of a change in circumstances or a determination that the designated party no longer meets the criteria for sanctions. The impact of this specific removal will depend on the identity and activities of the delisted entity.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. These actions aim to disrupt illicit networks that pose threats to international security and stability.

The designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating drug trafficking and terrorism financing globally. These measures typically result in the blocking of assets and prohibitions on transactions with the designated parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, International Criminal Court Designation, and Burma-related Designation Removal
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics. This settlement addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations, highlighting the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.

In separate actions, OFAC also announced a designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued associated General Licenses. Additionally, a Burma-related designation has been removed, indicating a specific adjustment to the sanctions program concerning Burma.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new Russia-related General License. This action provides specific authorization for certain transactions or activities that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.

General Licenses are often issued to facilitate humanitarian aid, certain financial transactions, or other activities deemed to be in the U.S. national interest, while maintaining the broader sanctions framework. Entities involved in Russia-related dealings should review the new license carefully.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a settlement agreement with Bank of America, N.A., resulting in a civil monetary penalty of $11,662,930. This penalty is part of broader enforcement actions against the bank for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws.

The violations stem from deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA)/anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program, which led to failures in monitoring and reporting suspicious transactions. The OCC also assessed a separate $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America for its deficient BSA/AML compliance program.

This settlement highlights the critical importance of robust compliance frameworks for financial institutions to prevent illicit financial activities and adhere to U.S. sanctions regulations. The Treasury Department emphasized that these actions represent some of the largest penalties in its history.

articles.headline: BIS Removes Two Addresses for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from Entity List
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has revised the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This rule is effective August 21, 2026.

This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025. The Entity List identifies entities for which there is reasonable cause to believe they are involved in activities contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States.

The removal of these addresses indicates a reassessment by the End-User Review Committee (ERC) regarding the entities' involvement in activities contrary to U.S. interests. Companies should regularly check for updates to the Entity List to ensure compliance with export control regulations.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
